Subject: Egress proof & proxy handoff request for private endpoint

Hi Mina / David,

We're starting our network security review for the Redwood private endpoint deployment. Security needs confirmation of the exact hostnames (FQDNs) that your runtime will initiate TLS to from our VPC, and whether we can rely on SNI assertion (plus cert thumbprint) rather than a static IP allowlist. Attached is a CSV with our preferred process (acme-egress-request.csv).

High level ask: please provide the minimal set of FQDNs and a recommended acceptance pattern (SNI match, required cert thumbprint, and any proxy CONNECT behavior). If you require us to allow a NAT pool instead, please provide the IP range(s) and rotation cadence so we can request a firewall exception.

We also need to understand whether an internal transparent proxy (TLS-inspecting) will break anything — do you require end-to-end TLS (no MITM), or can a corporate TLS-inspection proxy be used with an allowlist?

Thanks — Tom

--
Tom Gray

Subject: Re: Egress proof & proxy handoff request for private endpoint

Tom — thanks for the clear ask and the CSV. Short answers up front:

- Preferred pattern: FQDN + TLS SNI assertion + server cert thumbprint (we can provide thumbprints). This is the most robust approach when customers run TLS-inspection proxies.
- Ports: 443 (HTTPS) only. No additional outbound ports required.
- Proxy behavior: Redwood supports both direct egress and CONNECT-through-corporate-proxy. If you present a CONNECT tunnel to our FQDNs (passthrough TLS), we validate SNI/cert on the server side and the connection is unaffected. If your proxy performs MITM/TLS-inspection, we recommend making an exception for the listed FQDNs (SNI+thumbprint), otherwise application-level signatures may fail.

I'm attaching our current canonical FQDN list (redwood-egress-fqdns.txt) and the runtime cert thumbprint file (redwood-egress-cert-thumbprint.txt). We do not guarantee fixed public IPs for hosted egress; private deployments can optionally request a reserved egress NAT pool at time of provisioning — if you opt for that we can provide a CIDR range and rotation SLA.

Next steps:
1) Network: confirm whether SNI + thumbprint is acceptable, or if you need a CIDR.
2) If you need CIDR, tell us if a /28 or /24 better fits your change control window and we will return options.
3) If TLS inspection is mandatory on your side, confirm which FQDNs you need an exception for and we can propose a short-term allowlist for validation.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call with your ops team to walk through the artifacts.

Best,
Mina
Sr Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Adding technical detail for Acme's network/security team. This is the set we'll use for private deployments unless you request reserved egress:

Canonical FQDNs (sample):
- runtime-us-west.rw.redwood.net
- kvcache-us-west.rw.redwood.net
- metrics-collector-us.rw.redwood.net
- fallback-us-west.rw.redwood.net

TLS / Proxy notes:
- TLS: TLS 1.2+; server cert pinned by SHA256 thumbprint (attached). We will not accept downgraded TLS.
- SNI assertion: we expect the client to include SNI matching one of the canonical FQDNs. If your proxy terminates TLS, ensure it re-issues certs that preserve the original SNI or configure a transparent pass-through for these hosts.
- CONNECT proxy: we support HTTP CONNECT. Client flows will establish a TLS session end-to-end if the proxy is configured for passthrough.
- Health checks/ports: 443 only; keepalive TCP. No ICMP requirements.

IP allowlist fallback:
- If you absolutely cannot rely on FQDN/SNI, we can provide a reserved NAT pool for the deployment. Example: 198.51.100.16/28 (ephemeral example — we will provide assigned CIDR at provisioning). Rotation cadence: typical rotation every 7–14 days unless you request static binding (additional contract).

Evidence/artifacts included:
- redwood-egress-fqdns.txt (authoritative hostname list)
- redwood-egress-cert-thumbprint.txt (sha256 cert fingerprints)
- short README describing proxy CONNECT vs TLS-inspection behavior (in Confluence)

If Acme requires we can also produce a PCAP and TLS handshake dump from a test session (redacted) to aid firewall/IDS tuning.

-David
David Kim
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Tom — quick summary and acceptance request from Acme Security:

Summary:
- Redwood prefers FQDN + TLS SNI assertion + server cert thumbprint as the canonical allowlist mechanism.
- Ports: 443 only.
- If your proxy performs TLS-inspection, please add an exception for the FQDNs listed in redwood-egress-fqdns.txt OR configure CONNECT passthrough for those names.
- If you cannot update proxy rules, Redwood can provide a reserved egress CIDR during provisioning (requires a short operational SLA and potential additional charge).

Action items for Acme Security / Network Ops:
1) Please reply to this thread confirming one of the following choices:
   - A: Accept SNI + thumbprint model (preferred)
   - B: Require reserved egress CIDR (please indicate desired prefix size: /28 or /24)
   - C: Require a short trial where we run a test session and you approve firewall/IDS signatures after reviewing the test artifacts
2) If selecting A or C, confirm a target 30-minute slot next week for a joint network handshake (suggest Tue/Wed morning PT).

We appreciate the quick turn here — if you confirm option A we will treat the FQDN+thumbprint file as the authoritative artifact for your change window.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
